A short ceremonial straight sword in a closed dark scabbard, never drawn at a feast or audience. No snakes, no horns, no wings and no farr. A deep turquoise long-sleeved robe over an ivory dress, a dark lapis shawl around her shoulders, a narrow plain gold belt and small pearl earrings. No tall crown, no armour, no weapon and no halo. Her gestures are composed and deliberate, with one open palm when counselling or negotiating. She is distinct from young Rudabeh's two long black braids and malachite robe. All jewellery is muted, dimmer than the painting's central light.

Very long black hair in two heavy braids, never brown or white. An ivory long-sleeved dress beneath a malachite-green silk outer robe with a narrow turquoise hem, a slim gold belt and small pearl earrings. A fine gold fillet with one tiny unlettered turquoise disc, no tall crown, no armour and no weapon. Her posture is upright and calm. Gold jewellery stays dimmer than the central light; she is never a large portrait.
